forecast-period.text: A high pressure system centred in the Bight, is slowly drifting to the southeast to be located west of Tasmania on Saturday and in the Tasman Sea on Monday. A ridge of high pressure is expected to remain over South Australia. A trough over QLD pushes into the far northeast of SA from later Saturday through to later Monday. A trough of low pressure moves in the far west of South Australia later on Tuesday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Morning fog patches about the agricultural area. Isolated light showers about agricultural areas, most likely about windward coasts and ranges. Showers about the northwest, with possible thunderstorms about the far northwest. Maximum temperatures below average, tending near average about the southern agricultural area. Southeast to northeasterly winds.

Isolated light showers about the southern agricultural area, most likely about windward coasts and ranges. Isolated showers and possible thunderstorms in the far northwest corner during the afternoon and evening. East to southeasterly winds, although west to southwesterly about the southeast until evening.

Possible morning fog about the southeast and far west. Areas of frost inland about the agricultural area and south of the pastoral districts. Isolated showers about the north and west. Maximum temperatures below average. Southeast to northeasterly winds.

Possible morning fog on and east of the ranges and the far west. Showers about the North East Pastoral and Flinders districts possibly extending into the Mid North and parts of Eyre Peninsula, tending to rain at times in the northeast. Possible thunderstorms about the North East Pastoral district. Maximum temperatures below average in the north, grading to above average about the southern agricultural area. East to northeasterly winds.

text.p: Showers extending statewide. Possible thunderstorms about the far west. Maximum temperatures near to above average. Northeast to northerly winds, freshening in the west ahead of a southwesterly change in the far west.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Tuesday: Broad falls of less than 3 mm across much of the state, with isolated falls of 2 to 5 mm about the agricultural area with possible falls of 5 to 15 mm about the Pastoral and Flinders districts. Isolated falls of 15 to 30 mm possible about the northeast.
